newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan oil monopoly Dec profit down on high costs.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan oil monopoly Dec profit down on high costs.

text.p: Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Wednesday it had a pre-tax loss of T$1.323 billion in December, well short of a targeted T$1.595 billion profit.
December was the last month before an average nine percent domestic price increase on petroleum products took effect on January 1.
"Chinese Petroleum failed to meet its planned December pre-tax profit due to higher-than-budgeted international oil prices during the period," a company official said.
Chinese Petroleum December oil import costs averaged US$22.21 per barrel, much higher than budgeted US$15.26 per barrel, figures released by the company showed.
The company imported 24.7 million barrels of oil in December. Total imports in the July-December period were 116.4 million barrels.
Chinese Petroleum has an accumulated deficit of T$11.044 billion from its July to December fiscal budget.

Under strong pressure to reduce its deficit, Chinese Petroleum petitioned the government in December for an increase and was granted permission for an average nine percent hike that took effect on January 1. -- Taipei Newsroom (2-5080815)
